2026-01-04.headline: Cloud-native Windows endpoint starter guidance was simplified
2026-01-04.overview: The only recorded change removes introductory material from the cloud-native Windows endpoint tutorial: its comparison with Windows in cloud configuration and the embedded Windows 10 support notice. This is a documentation refinement rather than a service or policy change.
2026-01-04.adminImpact: Review internal links and onboarding guides that use this tutorial, especially where they explain when to choose a custom cloud-native configuration versus Windows in cloud configuration. Existing device configurations are unaffected.

keyChanges.title: Cloud-native Windows endpoint tutorial removes legacy orientation content
keyChanges.detail: The guide no longer compares its five-phase tutorial with Windows in cloud configuration and no longer carries the included Windows 10 support notice. The practical setup phases remain, but the introductory framing is leaner.

2026-01-05.headline: New driver and Hotpatch guidance sharpens Windows update planning
2026-01-05.overview: Windows update management dominates the day. New Intune guidance explains driver update approvals and a separate quality update policy introduces Hotpatch deployment requirements, while related update and co-management documentation was refreshed.
2026-01-05.adminImpact: For driver-update pilots, decide whether recommended drivers should be automatically approved or reviewed manually, and validate Autopatch licensing before assignment. For Hotpatch, confirm Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2-or-later eligibility, baseline currency, VBS, and the additional CHPE handling required for Arm64 devices.

keyChanges.title: Windows Driver Update Management policy guidance added
keyChanges.detail: The new guide describes automatic approval of recommended drivers, manual approval of every driver, and per-driver pause or reapproval. It also makes clear that only approved, newer drivers install and that the policy relies on Intune and Windows Autopatch.

keyChanges.title: Windows quality update policy documents Hotpatch prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new policy guide positions Hotpatch as an Autopatch-enabled way to install monthly security updates without a restart. It documents the Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 baseline, VBS, and Arm64 CHPE requirements, and notes that ineligible devices receive the normal cumulative update.

keyChanges.title: Intune roadmap adds management and assignment-filter signals
keyChanges.detail: The in-development guidance adds a planned Lenovo Device Orchestration portal link, Android settings-catalog filtering by management mode, Apple declarative device management assignment filters, and more managed-app filter values for Android and iOS/iPadOS.

2026-01-06.headline: Driver controls, update reporting, and AVD elevation support come into focus
2026-01-06.overview: The day adds practical boundaries for Windows driver update management, clarifies the diagnostic-data dependency for feature-update reporting, and updates EPM support information for Azure Virtual Desktop. A Message Center post also previews new Managed Home Screen permissions in built-in roles.
2026-01-06.adminImpact: Pilot driver updates through rings and avoid overlapping driver policies: assignment filters, Autopilot use, and policy-based rollback are not available. Enable the required diagnostic-data configuration before relying on update reports, assess EPM policies on supported single-session AVD, and review School Administrator and Help Desk Operator assignments ahead of the Managed Home Screen permission change.

keyChanges.title: Driver update FAQ defines operational guardrails
keyChanges.detail: The new FAQ confirms that driver policies do not support assignment filters or Windows Autopilot, do not provide rollback, and are clearer when a device receives one policy. It recommends staged rings, monitoring, and pausing updates where early-ring issues appear.

keyChanges.title: Feature-update reports emphasize diagnostic data prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The reporting documentation now explicitly requires sharing Windows diagnostic data with Intune at Required level or higher to show full device status and event reporting for feature updates.

keyChanges.title: EPM supports Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs
keyChanges.detail: Endpoint Privilege Management support information now includes Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines, enabling EPM onboarding and elevation-policy planning for that supported VDI configuration.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen permissions are planned for built-in roles
keyChanges.detail: School Administrator and Help Desk Operator will receive permissions to temporarily suspend and restore Managed Home Screen in the February release. The announcement recommends reviewing role assignments and documentation, though no immediate action is required.

2026-01-07.headline: Windows driver update prerequisites are standardized across the documentation
2026-01-07.overview: The day’s 40 changes are led by a reorganization of Windows driver update guidance. The documentation now presents its policy, licensing, platform, telemetry, reporting, cloud, and RBAC conditions more consistently, while Enterprise App Catalog guidance clarifies customer responsibility for catalogued apps.
2026-01-07.adminImpact: Compare active driver-update policies with the documented prerequisites: Intune Plan 1, a Windows license with Autopatch entitlement, supported Windows editions, diagnostic data, and public-cloud availability. Keep LTSC on update-ring management and do not assume catalogued third-party apps carry Microsoft assurances of compliance, authenticity, or integrity.

keyChanges.title: Driver update management documentation consolidates prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The refreshed overview explains that driver policies use Intune and Windows Autopatch, require supported licensing and device configuration, require diagnostic data for reporting, and are not available in GCC High or DoD. It directs administrators to policy configuration and reporting guidance.

keyChanges.title: Driver update prerequisite sections move to shared requirement content
keyChanges.detail: The main driver update article is restructured around reusable licensing, platform, device-configuration, tenant, and RBAC prerequisites. It reiterates that LTSC is not supported for driver, feature, or expedited quality updates and should use update rings instead.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog guidance clarifies customer assurance responsibilities
keyChanges.detail: The Enterprise App Management documentation now explicitly says Microsoft does not assert compliance, authorization, authenticity, or integrity for apps distributed through Intune. It also says manual validation for catalog updates can take up to seven days.

2026-01-08.headline: AVD elevation support and MDT retirement guidance stand out in update documentation
2026-01-08.overview: The day’s documentation refresh reorganizes Windows update prerequisites around the shared Autopatch model, explicitly adds EPM support information for single-session Azure Virtual Desktop, and reinforces the action required after Microsoft Deployment Toolkit retirement.
2026-01-08.adminImpact: For Windows update policies, confirm the common Autopatch prerequisites and preserve update-ring management for unsupported scenarios. Teams that still use MDT should plan to remove MDT task sequence steps and integration. EPM teams can evaluate single-session AVD, but should keep the scope to the documented supported configuration.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager documentation reinforces MDT retirement action
keyChanges.detail: The removed-and-deprecated features page links to MDT retirement guidance and reiterates that MDT integration with Configuration Manager and standalone MDT are no longer supported. Removing MDT task sequence steps before the integration is intended to prevent corruption and task-sequence modification failures.

keyChanges.title: EPM support is documented for Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs
keyChanges.detail: The in-development guidance says EPM elevation policies will work for users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines, extending the stated virtual-desktop support alongside the EPM Intune Suite capability.

keyChanges.title: Windows update documentation aligns shared Autopatch prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The Windows update index makes feature, quality, and driver update policies explicitly share the Windows Autopatch orchestration layer. It calls out Autopatch entitlement, Required diagnostic data, Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant availability, and the lack of support for Entra-registered devices in those policy types.

keyChanges.title: Driver update guidance is reorganized around approvals and prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The revised article separates approval controls from shared prerequisite content and makes policy configuration the next step, improving the operational path from eligibility validation through driver approval.

2026-01-09.headline: Windows update policy guidance makes rollout choices and prerequisites explicit
2026-01-09.overview: New feature and quality update policy guidance describes the choices administrators make between required and optional deployments, Hotpatch readiness, and expedited-update compatibility. The day’s broader MTD changes are largely documentation maintenance, while the material Windows update additions are operationally significant.
2026-01-09.adminImpact: Decide whether a feature update should require installation or let users opt in, and communicate optional deployments because users must select them in Windows Update. Before using Hotpatch or expedited updates, validate Autopatch-related prerequisites, remove conflicting Group Policy settings, and verify Update Health Tools on devices earlier than Windows 11 24H2.

keyChanges.title: Feature update policies gain required-versus-optional rollout guidance
keyChanges.detail: The new guide explains that a policy can hold a device to a chosen Windows version, expose the update as required or optional, and use rollout options for timing. Optional updates require Windows Autopatch licensing and need user action; changing between optional and required affects only devices that have not progressed too far into installation.

keyChanges.title: Quality update policy lists Hotpatch and expedite compatibility checks
keyChanges.detail: The new policy checklist points administrators to quality-update prerequisites and warns that preview builds, some update-ring choices, and Group Policy values such as WSUS location, Automatic Updates, feature deferral, and Disable Dual Scan can interfere with expedited deployment.

keyChanges.title: Expedited update guidance separates prerequisites from deployment behavior
keyChanges.detail: The updated documentation moves shared network, tenant, platform, device-configuration, and RBAC requirements into common content. It specifies that Update Health Tools remain necessary before Windows 11 24H2, while expedited policies still override quality deferrals for urgent servicing rather than normal monthly management.

2026-01-12.headline: Update ring controls receive a much clearer policy reference
2026-01-12.overview: The day’s 60 changes are concentrated in Windows update documentation. A new update-ring settings reference spells out the configuration choices for update delivery, restart behavior, and deadlines, while companion feature, quality, reporting, and Autopilot material is reorganized around the newer policy structure.
2026-01-12.adminImpact: Recheck production update rings against the new reference, particularly driver inclusion, deferral periods, automatic-install behavior, active hours, user pause and scan access, and deadline/grace-period settings. Education environments should note that the old Restart checks Skip behavior is intended for unattended cart devices, not one-to-one devices.

keyChanges.title: Update-ring policy settings get a comprehensive reference
keyChanges.detail: The new reference maps update-ring settings to their Windows CSPs and explains controls for Microsoft product updates, drivers, feature and quality deferrals, Windows 11 upgrade, uninstall periods, Insider builds, notifications, restart behavior, and enforcement deadlines.

keyChanges.title: Deadline and restart settings are framed as an end-user-experience choice
keyChanges.detail: The guidance documents the available install modes and the interaction of active hours, feature and quality deadlines, grace periods, and automatic reboot before the deadline. It recommends enabling pre-deadline automatic reboot to reduce the chance of a forced restart during active hours.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot known issues are refreshed alongside the update-policy work
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot known-issues documentation was updated as part of the broader refresh, giving administrators a current reference to consult before treating enrollment or reset behavior as a policy failure.

2026-01-13.headline: Hotpatch and expedited quality updates get their own operational playbooks
2026-01-13.overview: The Windows update documentation is further decomposed into focused guides for Hotpatch, expedited quality updates, driver-update policy, reporting, and quality-update management. The day also substantially refreshes the Defender for Endpoint–Intune compliance integration guidance.
2026-01-13.adminImpact: Use the dedicated Hotpatch and expedited-update guides when defining emergency servicing: Hotpatch is not a blanket replacement for standard quality-update planning, and expedited updates should be reserved for urgent releases. Revalidate the Defender connector and compliance-policy configuration against the refreshed integration instructions before troubleshooting compliance signals.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch guidance is separated from general quality-update policy
keyChanges.detail: A new guide presents Hotpatch as a distinct quality-update capability and groups its eligibility, deployment, and monitoring guidance with the Windows quality-update policy rather than leaving it embedded in broader update documentation.

keyChanges.title: Expedited Windows quality updates receive dedicated guidance
keyChanges.detail: The new expedite guide separates urgent quality-update deployment from normal servicing, making the policy’s scope, prerequisites, targeting, and reporting easier to use when responding to a security incident or out-of-band release.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint compliance integration documentation is substantially revised
keyChanges.detail: The refreshed integration guide consolidates how Intune uses the Defender for Endpoint connection for device-compliance evaluation and device onboarding, giving security and endpoint teams a single reference to validate their connector and policy design.

2026-01-14.headline: Expedited-update policy and phased feature rollout guidance become more explicit
2026-01-14.overview: A new expedited-update policy guide anchors the day’s Windows servicing changes. Feature-update and rollout documentation is expanded, and Advanced Analytics device-query guidance is refreshed, producing a clearer operational path from urgent patching through controlled version deployment and investigation.
2026-01-14.adminImpact: Use the dedicated expedited policy only for urgent quality updates and retain normal update rings for routine patching. When staging feature releases, keep version targeting in feature-update policy and review rollout controls rather than relying on overlapping ring deferrals that can delay or block the offer.

keyChanges.title: Expedited quality update policy gets a dedicated configuration guide
keyChanges.detail: The new guide isolates the setup and policy considerations for pushing an urgent Windows quality update, including the supporting prerequisites and operational constraints that distinguish expedited deployment from monthly servicing.

keyChanges.title: Feature update policy guidance is expanded
keyChanges.detail: The revised feature-update guidance strengthens the separation between controlling Windows version through feature-update policy and using update rings for user-experience controls, helping administrators avoid conflicting deferral settings during a migration to policy-based targeting.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics device query documentation is refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The multiple-device query guide receives a substantive update, keeping the investigation workflow current for teams using Advanced Analytics to collect and compare device information at scale.

2026-01-15.headline: Windows update and Edge for Business guidance are reorganized into task-focused guides
2026-01-15.overview: The 55 changes are chiefly a documentation reorganization. Windows update policy material is renamed and split into discrete driver, feature, and update-ring guides, while the Microsoft Edge for Business data-security sequence receives new end-user-experience and troubleshooting steps and retires obsolete pages.
2026-01-15.adminImpact: Update bookmarks, help-desk procedures, and training links that point to the previous plural policy pages or Edge guide step numbers. The product capabilities are not presented as new, but the task-oriented locations should become the support baseline. Admins also gain a centralized view of Device Offboarding tasks alongside other Intune work.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Edge for Business data-security troubleshooting is re-sequenced
keyChanges.detail: A new troubleshooting step replaces the older end-of-sequence page as part of the Edge for Business data-security documentation refresh. The companion security-baseline and end-user-experience pages are retired or renumbered, so internal documentation should follow the new sequence.

keyChanges.title: Windows driver, feature, and update-ring policies move to focused guides
keyChanges.detail: New task-focused policy pages replace older plural-named documentation, separating configuration guidance for driver updates, feature updates, and update-ring settings. This is primarily an information-architecture change, but it changes the canonical links administrators should use.

keyChanges.title: Centralized Admin tasks now include Device Offboarding work
keyChanges.detail: The Admin tasks documentation adds Device Offboarding tasks and points to their current admin-center location. The unified view is described as covering Device Offboarding, Endpoint Privilege Management, and other administrative work, governed by Organization Read permission.

2026-01-16.headline: Autopilot Reset known issue is the key operational signal amid quickstart refreshes
2026-01-16.overview: Most of the day’s changes modernize Intune evaluation and quickstart material, including Android compliance and app-protection walkthroughs. The standout operational item is a newly documented Windows Autopilot Reset limitation when a local-account network-deny policy is applied.
2026-01-16.adminImpact: If technicians use a local administrator to initiate Autopilot Reset, test any policy that sets Deny access to this computer from the network for the Local account. Remove that setting for the account or exclude devices that need local Reset until the issue is resolved. The refreshed quickstarts also identify the least-privilege roles and prerequisites for common evaluation tasks.

keyChanges.title: Local Autopilot Reset can fail for local administrators under a network-deny policy
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft documents that a local administrator cannot start local Windows Autopilot Reset when an Intune policy denies the Local account network access. The workaround is to remove the setting for that account or exclude reset-dependent devices, then allow the revised policy to sync.

keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise password compliance quickstart adopts explicit prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The revised walkthrough separates licensing and RBAC requirements, uses the Policy and Profile Manager role, and makes policy assignment and Conditional Access follow-up clearer for a basic Android password-compliance deployment.

keyChanges.title: App protection quickstart clarifies role and user-group requirements
keyChanges.detail: The updated app-protection walkthrough identifies the Application Manager role, prerequisite user, group, device, and app setup, and reiterates that app protection policies are assigned to user groups rather than device groups.

2026-01-20.headline: Intune adds remote control to suspend or restore Managed Home Screen
2026-01-20.overview: Two new Android remote-action guides introduce the ability to temporarily suspend Managed Home Screen and restore it later. The accompanying Autopilot device-preparation update is a documentation-link correction, while the substantive change is the new frontline-device recovery and support control.
2026-01-20.adminImpact: For Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and dedicated devices, confirm who should be able to bypass or reinstate the kiosk-style experience. Grant the dedicated Remote tasks permissions only to Help Desk Operator, School Administrator, or carefully scoped custom roles, and document when suspension is permitted.

keyChanges.title: Suspend Managed Home Screen becomes a remote device action
keyChanges.detail: Administrators can temporarily disable Managed Home Screen on supported Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and dedicated devices, returning users to the standard home screen and apps. The action requires the Temporarily Suspend Managed Home Screen remote-task permission.

keyChanges.title: Restore Managed Home Screen becomes a companion remote action
keyChanges.detail: Administrators can re-enable Managed Home Screen from the device overview after a suspension. Restoring returns the device to its managed-home-screen policies and restricted app and settings experience, using the Restore Managed Home Screen permission.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation clarifies its ESP independence
keyChanges.detail: The device-preparation what’s-new page corrects the link to the monthly security-update explanation and reiterates that Windows Autopilot device preparation does not use Enrollment Status Page, so the ESP quality-update setting does not apply to it.

2026-01-21.headline: Managed Home Screen actions receive Graph links and support caveats
2026-01-21.overview: The new Managed Home Screen remote actions are polished with direct Microsoft Graph action references. Related guidance adds a clear warning that deploying standalone Windows update packages as Win32 apps is an as-is workaround, and notes that Android battery optimization can prevent Intune notifications from arriving.
2026-01-21.adminImpact: Use the documented Graph actions rather than guessing endpoint names when automating Managed Home Screen recovery. Do not treat an MSU-as-Win32 deployment as a standard patch-management pattern; use supported Windows update policy instead. If notifications appear unreliable on Android, validate battery-optimization treatment for Company Portal or the Intune app.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen remote actions link to their Graph operations
keyChanges.detail: The restore and suspend guides now point to the restoreManagedHomeScreen and temporarilySuspendManagedHomeScreen Graph actions, alongside the managedDevice resource, giving automation teams the canonical operation names.

keyChanges.title: Win32 deployment of MSU packages is explicitly not recommended
keyChanges.detail: The Windows update-package article continues to describe packaging an MSU as a Win32 app, but now labels the approach as as-is and not a recommended way to deploy updates.

keyChanges.title: Custom notification guidance calls out Android battery optimization
keyChanges.detail: The documentation warns that device battery-optimization settings can prevent notification delivery and suggests disabling optimization for Company Portal or the Intune app where reliable notification delivery is required.

2026-01-22.headline: Migration planning and Conditional Access retirement create two 2026 action items
2026-01-22.overview: The updated Basic Mobility and Security migration guide makes license sequencing, policy replacement, and post-migration cleanup more concrete. Two Message Center notices add future deadlines: the Require approved client app Conditional Access control retires in June, and most Intune guided scenarios leave the admin center in March.
2026-01-22.adminImpact: Inventory Conditional Access policies that use Require approved client app and plan the transition to Require application protection policy before June 2026. For Basic Mobility and Security migrations, stage license assignment and replacement Intune policies carefully; Intune-licensed users can receive policies promptly, and old Basic Mobility and Security policies should be removed after migration. Preserve any guided-scenario documentation outside the product UI before March.

keyChanges.title: Basic Mobility and Security migration guidance emphasizes staged licensing and policy cleanup
keyChanges.detail: The revised guide says assigning Intune licenses switches users to Intune management and prepares them for new policies. It recommends confirming license capacity, reviewing and deleting unneeded Basic Mobility and Security policies, reviewing group membership, replacing policies in Intune, and removing old policies so they cannot be assigned accidentally later.

keyChanges.title: Require approved client app retires from Conditional Access in June
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft states that the Require approved client app control will retire in June 2026 and recommends Require application protection policy as the replacement. After retirement, the legacy control can no longer be enforced.

keyChanges.title: Most Intune guided scenarios are scheduled for removal in March
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center announcement says all guided scenarios except Windows 365 Boot will be removed from the Intune admin center in March 2026. Existing configurations remain in place, but teams should use the alternative guidance for future setup and training.

2026-01-23.headline: Intune migration and device-query docs clarify practical transition and query behavior
2026-01-23.overview: The Basic Mobility and Security migration guide receives further refinement, while Advanced Analytics documentation clarifies how the Device entity behaves in cross-device queries. Configuration Manager also updates the presentation guidance for high-impact task sequences in Software Center.
2026-01-23.adminImpact: Continue migration work in a staged order—licenses, policy mapping, groups, supported-device review, then replacement Intune policies—rather than assigning broad licenses before the target policies are ready. Query authors should review saved Kusto patterns that treat Device as a scalar and make property references explicit when filtering, sorting, or aggregating.

keyChanges.title: Migration guide further defines the Basic Mobility and Security transition sequence
keyChanges.detail: The updated guide frames the move as a preparation, policy-mapping, and replacement effort. It calls out license capacity, old-policy cleanup, assignment-group review, device support, and the risk that already licensed users can receive Intune policy earlier than planned.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics clarifies the Device entity in multi-device queries
keyChanges.detail: The documentation explains that Device is an entity-type column rather than a scalar value. Query authors should reference a specific property for scalar operations, such as Device.DeviceName for ordering or filtering, and should explicitly name aggregated expressions that they later reference.

keyChanges.title: High-impact task sequences are described by their Software Center placement
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager guidance clarifies that a deployment marked as a high-impact task sequence appears under the Operating Systems node in Software Center; without that designation it appears under Applications.

2026-01-24.headline: Defender for Android personal-profile protection ends in March; device queries need a join update
2026-01-24.overview: A Message Center announcement says Microsoft Defender for Android will stop protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices in March 2026, retaining the corporate work-profile focus. The accompanying Advanced Analytics documentation changes also make an actionable query-compatibility correction for Device joins.
2026-01-24.adminImpact: Identify Android users and processes that expect Defender protection in enrolled personal profiles and adjust communications, security expectations, or enrollment design before March. Review saved Device Query scripts now: joins written as on Device.DeviceId must move to on Device or omit the clause when joining on the Device entity.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Android ends enrolled personal-profile protection in March
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft will focus Defender for Android protection on corporate work profiles and end support for enrolled personal profiles by March 2026. The announcement says work profiles and unenrolled devices are not affected.

keyChanges.title: Device Query joins using Device.DeviceId are no longer supported
keyChanges.detail: Advanced Analytics documentation says queries that join on Device.DeviceId should use on Device instead, or omit the on clause when joining on the Device entity. The update also reinforces using scalar device properties, such as serial number or OS version, in distinct, summarize, and order-by operations.

2026-01-26.headline: Cloud PKI receives a standalone operational documentation set
2026-01-26.overview: Eight new Cloud PKI articles establish a dedicated documentation area for architecture, deployment models, CA configuration, bring-your-own CA, monitoring, audit logs, and deletion. The content largely relocates and modernizes existing guidance, but it makes certificate-service planning much easier to navigate.
2026-01-26.adminImpact: Use the new Cloud PKI paths as the canonical source for certificate-service runbooks. Before deploying BYOCA, validate the CA hierarchy, tenant role permissions, supported EKUs, root/issuing CA design, SCEP profiles, and required Intune endpoints. Update any bookmarks that still point to the former protection-area Cloud PKI paths.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI adds a documented bring-your-own CA model
keyChanges.detail: The BYOCA guide describes creating a Cloud PKI issuing CA anchored to an on-premises or private CA, including the certificate-signing-request process, CA permissions, root-source selection, EKU restrictions, and SCEP profile follow-up.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI root and issuing CA configuration is moved to dedicated guidance
keyChanges.detail: The new configuration article explains how a tenant root CA becomes the trust anchor for issuing CAs, including selectable validity periods, EKU constraints, subject attributes, and the relationship between root-CA and issuing-CA capabilities.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI deployment models are catalogued in a new guide
keyChanges.detail: A dedicated deployment-model reference now helps administrators distinguish Microsoft-managed and bring-your-own-root CA designs before creating certificate profiles and issuing CAs.

2026-01-27.headline: App protection, enrollment, and tenant guidance receive maintenance updates
2026-01-27.overview: The day’s 14 changes are primarily documentation maintenance across app-protection monitoring, Windows enrollment, service description, and tenant sign-up material. No new platform capability or immediate configuration change is evidenced in the tracked updates.
2026-01-27.adminImpact: No emergency tenant action is indicated. Use the refreshed documentation when updating onboarding or app-protection monitoring runbooks, but treat this as a maintenance release rather than a policy-change event.

keyChanges.title: App protection policy monitoring guidance is refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The monitoring article receives a small documentation update, keeping the current reference for reviewing app protection policy status and troubleshooting results.

keyChanges.title: Windows enrollment guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The Windows enrollment article is revised as part of a broader onboarding documentation refresh, so administrators should prefer its current steps when maintaining enrollment runbooks.

2026-01-28.headline: Configuration Manager developer and reference pages undergo a broad maintenance pass
2026-01-28.overview: All 92 tracked changes are Configuration Manager documentation updates, heavily concentrated in SDK, WMI, migration, software-update, hierarchy, and log-file reference material. The evidence shows a bulk reference and publishing cleanup rather than a newly announced Configuration Manager feature.
2026-01-28.adminImpact: No tenant-wide change is indicated. Configuration Manager developers and automation owners should use the refreshed reference pages when validating scripts, WMI calls, migration logic, and software-update integrations, but no rollout or policy change is required solely because of this documentation pass.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager migration API reference is refreshed
keyChanges.detail: Migration mapping methods such as CheckDecommissionState, CleanupHierarchyData, Decommission, and ExcludeAndInclude are among the revised reference pages, providing updated source material for custom migration tooling.

keyChanges.title: Software-update WMI reference content is included in the maintenance set
keyChanges.detail: The update includes classes and methods used to inspect update compliance, deployment, source, package, and synchronization state, reinforcing the current reference base for scripted Configuration Manager operations.

2026-01-29.headline: Defender integration steps and Configuration Manager SQL requirements are clarified
2026-01-29.overview: A large revision to the Defender for Endpoint–Intune integration guide makes the portal connection and onboarding process more explicit. Configuration Manager SQL Server requirements are also consolidated into a clearer set of server and database settings, alongside routine app-management documentation maintenance.
2026-01-29.adminImpact: Validate the Defender connection from Intune before reconfiguring it: if it already reports Enabled, move directly to onboarding or policy work. For Configuration Manager SQL maintenance, do not alter the documented required database settings without Microsoft support; compare support and recovery procedures against the new consolidated configuration table.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint connection instructions are reorganized around connection status
keyChanges.detail: The refreshed guide begins by checking Endpoint security > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint in Intune, then directs unconnected tenants to enable Microsoft Intune connection in Defender XDR Settings > Endpoints > General > Advanced features. It also clarifies the current portal navigation and onboarding references.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager SQL Server requirements are consolidated
keyChanges.detail: The revised support guide lists required server and database configurations—such as CLR, nested triggers, change tracking, Service Broker, snapshot settings, ANSI settings, and TRUSTWORTHY—and says not to alter them unless Microsoft support instructs otherwise.

2026-01-30.headline: End-of-month updates are largely reference and link maintenance
2026-01-30.overview: The 21 changes include small updates to Edge management, Configuration Manager SQL support and prerequisite checklists, RBAC, device scopes, Autopilot device preparation, and remote-action documentation. Managed Home Screen action pages are removed from their standalone locations, continuing the recent documentation reorganization.
2026-01-30.adminImpact: No immediate service action is evidenced. Refresh support links for Managed Home Screen and Windows update-package deployment, and use the current RBAC, device-scope, and Configuration Manager prerequisite documentation during planned maintenance rather than treating the updates as a feature rollout.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Edge management documentation is refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The Edge management guide receives an update as part of the app-management documentation maintenance set, providing the current reference for Intune administrators managing Microsoft Edge.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager SQL Server support documentation is updated
keyChanges.detail: The SQL Server support reference is revised alongside prerequisite and update-installation checklists, making it the preferred source when planning Configuration Manager database or version maintenance.

2026-01-31.headline: Cloud PKI CA expiration now has a concrete replacement runbook
2026-01-31.overview: New Cloud PKI guidance explains how to avoid certificate-issuance disruption when an issuing CA approaches expiration. Endpoint Privilege Management documentation also makes the child-process elevation choices and their security implications more explicit.
2026-01-31.adminImpact: Treat CA expiration as a customer-managed continuity task: create a replacement issuing CA with matching root source, EKUs, and key sizes, then replace the SCEP URI in every affected profile. Do not add a second URI and do not assume changing the URI reissues certificates. For EPM, review child-process settings and avoid broad rules around shells or script engines.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI CA expiration guidance requires replacement CA and SCEP profile updates
keyChanges.detail: If an issuing CA expires, profiles using it cannot issue new certificates, risking Wi-Fi, VPN, email, corporate-resource, and certificate-authentication failures. Microsoft says administrators must create a new issuing CA and replace the old SCEP URI in each affected profile; Microsoft cannot do this automatically.

keyChanges.title: EPM explains child-process elevation behavior and the safer default
keyChanges.detail: Elevation rules can require each child process to meet its own rule, deny all child elevation, or allow children to inherit elevation. The documentation warns that inherited elevation skips child rule and deny-rule evaluation, and recommends avoiding broad rules for shells and script engines.

2026-02-02.headline: Custom RBAC guidance adds Admin tasks permissions and Android kiosk support is clarified
2026-02-02.overview: The day updates custom-role documentation and Managed Home Screen OEMConfig guidance. The material makes the permissions behind centralized administrative tasks more visible and extends two Managed Home Screen permissions to an additional supported Android management scenario.
2026-02-02.adminImpact: If you use custom roles, review whether operators who manage centralized Admin tasks need the new Create, Read, Update, or Delete permissions—do not grant them by default. For Managed Home Screen, validate Alarms & Reminders and Write Settings behavior on the documented Android device modes before changing OEMConfig permissions.

keyChanges.title: Custom roles can be scoped to centralized Admin tasks
keyChanges.detail: The custom-role permission reference adds Admin tasks Create, Delete, Read, and Update operations, enabling least-privilege delegation for device-management administrative task creation, status updates, and review.

For gradual feature rollouts, verify the timing and cloud-processing prerequisite. For Win32 scripts, observe the 50 KB, silent-execution, return-code, and Multi-Admin Approval constraints. With Multi-Admin Approval enabled, scripts cannot be uploaded during app creation; create the app first, then add or modify the script. The documentation does not state preview or GA‌

2026-01.headline: January reset the Windows servicing playbook and surfaced key 2026 migration deadlines
2026-01.overview: January recorded 666 changes and four Message Center announcements. The month rebuilt Windows servicing guidance around focused driver, feature, quality, Hotpatch, expedited-update, update-ring, report, and rollout-policy pages. It also established Cloud PKI operational guidance, documented CA-expiration recovery, expanded EPM support and rule clarity, and announced upcoming changes to Conditional Access, Intune guided scenarios, and Defender for Android personal profiles.
2026-01.adminImpact: Prioritize four workstreams: refresh Windows servicing runbooks and pilots using the focused policy guides; migrate Conditional Access policies away from Require approved client app before June; plan the March changes to guided scenarios and Defender Android personal-profile coverage; and establish a tested Cloud PKI CA-replacement process before any issuing CA approaches expiration. Also remove remaining MDT task-sequence dependencies and review local Autopilot Reset policy conflicts.

keyChanges.title: Windows update management documentation shifts to focused policy guides
keyChanges.detail: The month introduces or reorganizes separate guidance for driver updates, feature updates, quality updates, Hotpatch, expedited updates, update rings, reports, and rollout options. The material clarifies shared Autopatch prerequisites and recommends staged operational control instead of overlapping policy patterns.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager administrators are reminded to remove retired MDT integration
keyChanges.detail: MDT integration and standalone MDT are no longer supported. Documentation directs teams to remove MDT task-sequence steps before removing the integration, to prevent task-sequence corruption and modification failures.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI gains BYOCA, deployment, and expiration guidance
keyChanges.detail: The new documentation set covers building and operating Cloud PKI, including a BYOCA issuing CA anchored to a private CA. A CA-expiration guide later makes the customer-managed replacement and SCEP-profile update procedure explicit.

keyChanges.title: Three announced deadlines require roadmap attention
keyChanges.detail: Require approved client app retires from Conditional Access in June 2026; most Intune guided scenarios leave the admin center in March; and Defender for Android ends enrolled personal-profile protection in March while retaining corporate work-profile focus.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint operations gain new control and safety guidance
keyChanges.detail: The month adds suspend and restore actions for Managed Home Screen, lists EPM support for single-session AVD, clarifies EPM child-process elevation risk, and documents a local Autopilot Reset failure caused by a local-account network-deny policy.
